title: The Jacobian over a separably closed field
statement:
Let $k$ be a separably closed field and let $C$ be a
smooth projective curve over $k$
which is geometrically integral,
of genus $g=g(C)=\dim_kH^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$ ([def-pc-genus]). There is
an abelian variety $J_C$ over
$k$, the *Jacobian* of $C$ in the sense of [def-sc-jacobian], of dimension $g$, together
with a natural isomorphism of group-valued functors

$$
\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\cong h_{J_C},
$$

where $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ is the degree-zero part of the
Picard functor; its $k$-points are the
invertible modules of degree $0$ on $C$, and for algebraically closed
$k$ they are the $\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)$ of [def-sc-pic0], so that
$\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)=J_C(k)$ canonically in that case. Moreover $J_C$
is compatible with base change along extensions of separably closed fields:
$J_{C_{k'}}\cong(J_C)_{k'}$ for $k\subseteq k'$ separably closed.
The scope of this result, and the case of a general ground field, are
discussed in a remark below in this chapter.

proof.text: *(1) The Jacobian as a representing object.* By [thm-pc-picard-representable] the Picard functor $\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ of [def-pc-picard-functor] is represented by a scheme $\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}_{C/k}$ which is a group scheme over $k$, its group law being the one induced by the group-valued functor $\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ (tensor product of invertible modules) through the Yoneda lemma; on affine $k$-schemes $\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ is the functor of [def-sc-picard-functor] by [lem-pc-picard-functor-agrees-sc]. Fix a $k$-rational point $P$ of $C$ (see step (6)). By [prop-pd-picard-degree-decomposition] (2) and (3), the subfunctor $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ of classes of fibrewise degree $0$ is represented by the open and closed subgroup scheme $J:=\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}^0_{C/k}$ of $\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}_{C/k}$; write $\varphi:\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\xrightarrow{\sim}h_J$ for the representing isomorphism. Since the group law of $J$ is the restriction of that of $\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}_{C/k}$ and $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\subseteq\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ is a subgroup functor ([prop-pd-picard-degree-decomposition] (1)), $\varphi$ is an isomorphism of group-valued functors.

source.place: Tag 0BA0 (lemma-picard-pieces), proof, first paragraph (decomposition Pic_{X/k,sigma} = coprod Pic^d, the scheme exists by Proposition 0B9Z) and clause (3)

proof.text: *(2) Commutativity.* For every $k$-scheme $T$ the group $\operatorname{Pic}(C_T)$ is abelian (the tensor product of invertible modules is commutative up to canonical isomorphism), so the degree-zero subgroups, the presheaf they form and its fppf sheafification $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ ([prop-pd-picard-degree-decomposition] (1)) are abelian group-valued. Through the group isomorphism $\varphi$ of step (1) the group $J(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_k(T,J)$ is abelian for every $T$; taking $T=J\times_kJ$ and the point $(\mathrm{pr}_1,\mathrm{pr}_2)$ gives $m\circ s=m$ for the swap $s$, i.e. $J$ is a commutative group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme].

source.place: proof, paragraph 'Connected and commutative': 'The group law is the tensor product of invertible modules (Yoneda), which is commutative'

proof.text: *(3) Proper and smooth of dimension $g$.* By the theorem of the base [thm-sc-theorem-of-the-base], $\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}^0_{C/k}=J$ is proper over $k$ and smooth over $k$ of dimension $g=\dim_kH^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$ [def-pc-genus].

source.place: Tag 0BA0 (lemma-picard-pieces), clause (1) and its proof (smoothness of dimension g from Hilb^g; properness from the surjectivity of gamma_d for d >= g and translation)

proof.text: *(4) Connectedness.* By [lem-sc-picg-geometrically-integral] the scheme $\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}^g_{C/k}$ representing the degree-$g$ part $\operatorname{Pic}^g_{C/k}$ (which exists by [prop-pd-picard-degree-decomposition] (2)) is geometrically integral over $k$. By [prop-pd-picard-degree-decomposition] (4), translation by the $k$-point $[\mathcal O_C(gP)]$ is an isomorphism of $k$-schemes $J=\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}^0_{C/k}\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}^g_{C/k}$; it base changes to isomorphisms $J_{k'}\cong(\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}^g_{C/k})_{k'}$ for every field extension $k'/k$, so $J$ is geometrically integral over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. In particular $J$ is integral, hence irreducible, and it is nonempty (it contains the unit $e$, the class of $\mathcal O_C$); an irreducible space is connected, so $J$ is connected.

source.place: proof, paragraph 'Connected and commutative' ('Hilb^g is an irreducible variety, so its image Pic^g under alpha is irreducible') together with the second paragraph ('Pic^0 is isomorphic to Pic^g (translation by O_C(gP)), so it suffices to prove the geometric properties for Pic^g'); Stacks Tag 0BA0 clause (1) ('varieties')

proof.text: *(5) $J$ is a Jacobian.* By steps (1)–(4), $J$ is a group scheme over $k$ which is proper, smooth and connected, i.e. an abelian variety over $k$ [def-sc-abelian-variety], commutative, of dimension $g$; together with the isomorphism of group-valued functors $\varphi:\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\xrightarrow{\sim}h_J$ of step (1) the pair $(J,\varphi)$ is a Jacobian of $C$ in the sense of [def-sc-jacobian]. Put $J_C:=J$.

source.place: proof, first paragraph 'Why this is the Jacobian'

proof.text: *(6) The $k$-points.* $C$ is nonempty and smooth over the separably closed field $k$, so it has a $k$-rational point $P$ [lem-pc-rational-points-dense]. By [lem-pc-rational-hyp], $f:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ with the section $P$ satisfies the hypotheses of [thm-pc-pic-split]; applied with $T=\operatorname{Spec}k$ (so $C_T=C$), the sequence $0\to\operatorname{Pic}(\operatorname{Spec}k)\to\operatorname{Pic}(C)\to\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}(\operatorname{Spec}k)\to0$ is exact, and $\operatorname{Pic}(\operatorname{Spec}k)=0$ because an invertible module on the spectrum of a field is free of rank one. So the map $\operatorname{Pic}(C)\to\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}(k)$, $\mathcal L\mapsto$ the class of $\mathcal L$, is a group isomorphism. The only point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ has residue field $k$, so the fibrewise degree [def-pd-fibrewise-degree] of $\mathcal L$ is $\deg_C(\mathcal L)=\chi(C,\mathcal L)-\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)$ [def-pc-degree-line-bundle], and on every geometric fibre $C_{\bar K}$ it is $\deg_{C_{\bar K}}(\mathcal L_{\bar K})=\deg_C(\mathcal L)$ by [lem-pc-degree-base-change] (1). Hence $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}(k)$ corresponds to the subgroup $\{\mathcal L\in\operatorname{Pic}(C):\deg_C\mathcal L=0\}$, the invertible modules of degree $0$, and composing with $\varphi$ gives a group isomorphism $\{\mathcal L\in\operatorname{Pic}(C):\deg_C\mathcal L=0\}\cong J(k)$ (a group isomorphism because $\varphi$ is one of group-valued functors and $\operatorname{Pic}(C)\to\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}(k)$ is a homomorphism).

source.place: proof, paragraph 'Points and base change': 'By [sk-prop-picard-pic-split] with T=Spec k and Pic(Spec k)=0, Pic_{C/k}(k)=Pic(C), and J(C)(k) is its degree-zero part'; Stacks Tag 0BA0 clause (2)

proof.text: *(7) Comparison with $\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)$ for algebraically closed $k$.* Let $k$ be algebraically closed. By [lem-pc-curves-are-sc], $C$ is a smooth connected curve in the sense of [def-sc-curves], so $\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)=\ker(\deg)$ of [def-sc-pic0] is defined: there $\deg$ is defined on $\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ by transporting the divisor degree across the identification $\operatorname{Cl}(C)\cong\operatorname{Pic}(C)$, $D\mapsto[\mathcal O_C(D)]$, which that definition fixes. Let $\mathcal L\in\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ and let $D$ be the divisor class corresponding to $[\mathcal L]$ under this identification, so that $\mathcal L\cong\mathcal O_C(D)$ and, by the definition, $\deg[\mathcal L]=\deg D$; and writing $D=D_1-D_2$ with $D_1,D_2$ effective, $\mathcal O_C(D)\otimes\mathcal O_C(D_2)\cong\mathcal O_C(D_1)$. By [lem-pc-degree-base-change] (2) (tensor with an effective divisor) $\deg_C\mathcal O_C(D_1)=\deg_C\mathcal O_C(D)+\deg_C\mathcal O_C(D_2)$, and by [lem-pc-degree-agrees-sc] $\deg_C\mathcal O_C(D_i)=\deg D_i$ for the effective $D_i$. Hence $\deg_C\mathcal L=\deg D_1-\deg D_2=\deg D=\deg[\mathcal L]$: the degree of step (6) agrees with that of [def-sc-pic0], and the subgroup of step (6) is $\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)$. So $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}(k)=\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)=J_C(k)$ canonically.

source.place: ## Proof, step (1) 'The Picard functor': 'for k algebraically closed, C is a smooth connected curve in the sense of [def-sc-pic0] by [lem-pc-curves-are-sc], and Pic^0_{C/k}(k)=Pic^0(C)'

proof.text: *(8) Base change.* Let $k\subseteq k'$ be an extension of separably closed fields. By [prop-pc-xk-integral] (2) (with the rational point $P$ of step (6)) $C_{k'}$ is a smooth projective curve over $k'$ with $\dim_{k'}H^1(C_{k'},\mathcal O_{C_{k'}})=g$, and it is geometrically integral over $k'$ because $(C_{k'})_{k''}=C_{k''}$ for every extension $k''/k'$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]; so the Jacobian $J_{C_{k'}}$ exists by steps (1)–(5) over $k'$. The base change $J_{k'}$ is a commutative group scheme over $k'$ (base change of $m,i,e$), proper and smooth over $k'$ [lem-pc-proper-base-change], of dimension $\dim J=g$ (cover $J$, which is of finite type over $k$, by finitely many affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$; then $J_{k'}$ is covered by the $\operatorname{Spec}(A_i\otimes_kk')$, and $\dim(A_i\otimes_kk')=\dim A_i$ by [lem-pc-dim-base-change]), and connected, being integral by step (4); so it is an abelian variety of dimension $g$ over $k'$. For a $k'$-scheme $T$, $h_{J_{k'}}(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_{k'}(T,J_{k'})=\operatorname{Hom}_k(T,J)\cong\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}(T)$ by $\varphi$, naturally in $T$ and compatibly with the group laws, and $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ restricted to $k'$-schemes is $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C_{k'}/k'}$ by [cor-pd-pic0-base-change]. So $J_{k'}$ with the composite isomorphism $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C_{k'}/k'}\cong h_{J_{k'}}$ is a Jacobian of $C_{k'}$ [def-sc-jacobian], and by the uniqueness of Jacobians [lem-sc-jacobian-unique] $J_{C_{k'}}\cong(J_C)_{k'}$.

Let $k$ be a separably closed field and let $C$ be a
$k$-scheme which is proper and smooth of relative dimension $1$ over $k$
and geometrically integral,
of genus $g=g(C)=\dim_kH^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$ ([def-pc-genus]). There is
an abelian variety $J_C$ over
$k$, the *Jacobian* of $C$ in the sense of [def-sc-jacobian], of dimension $g$, together
with a natural isomorphism of group-valued functors

$$
\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\cong h_{J_C},
$$

where $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ is the degree-zero part of the
Picard functor; its $k$-points are the
invertible modules of degree $0$ on $C$, and for algebraically closed
$k$ they are the $\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)$ of [def-sc-pic0], so that
$\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)=J_C(k)$ canonically in that case. Moreover $J_C$

$J_{C_{k'}}\cong(J_C)_{k'}$ for $k\subseteq k'$ separably closed.

proof.text:
[thm-pc-picard-representable] of the Picard chapter – the Picard functor
of a smooth projective curve over a separably closed field is
representable, with the full decomposition carried out there (*reference: Stacks Project, Picard Schemes of Curves, Proposition 44.6.6, [Tag 0B9Z](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B9Z)*); cf. Mumford, Abelian Varieties; Milne, Abelian Varieties, Ch. 12. We outline the
classical construction; the existence and property statements are
theorems of the sources above.

*(0) Projectivity.* Since a scheme which is proper over a field and of dimension $1$ is projective over it,
$C$ is a smooth projective curve ([def-pc-smooth-projective-curve]), and it
is geometrically integral by hypothesis; so the results for smooth
projective curves cited below apply to $C$.

*(1) The Picard functor.* $\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ and
$\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}\subseteq\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ are
as in [def-sc-picard-functor]; for $k$ algebraically closed, $C$ is a
smooth connected curve in the sense of [def-sc-pic0] by
[lem-pc-curves-are-sc], and
$\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}(k)=\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)$ of
[def-sc-pic0].

*(2) Representability.* The theorem of Grothendieck states
that $\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ (which is the functor of [def-pc-picard-functor] by [lem-pc-picard-functor-agrees-sc]) is represented by a group scheme
locally of finite type over $k$ ([thm-pc-picard-representable] of the Picard chapter; *reference: Stacks Project, Picard Schemes of Curves, Proposition 44.6.6, [Tag 0B9Z](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B9Z)*). The
subfunctor $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ is represented by an open
and closed subgroup scheme ([prop-pd-picard-degree-decomposition],
parts (2) and (3)).

*(3) Smoothness and the tangent space.* By
[lem-sc-pic-tangent-space], the tangent space of
$\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ at the identity is
$H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$, of dimension $g$ ([def-pc-genus]);
by [thm-sc-theorem-of-the-base],
$\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ is a disjoint union of smooth
varieties of dimension $g$.

*(4) Properness.* $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ is proper by
[thm-sc-theorem-of-the-base] (the ``theorem of the base'').

*(5) Abelian variety and base change.* By (2)–(4),
$J_C:=\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$ is a proper smooth connected
group scheme, i.e. an abelian variety
([def-sc-abelian-variety]), of dimension $g$. For
$k$ algebraically closed, $J_C(k)=\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)$
([def-sc-picard-functor], [def-sc-pic0]) by
representability, and base change
compatibility $J_{C_{k'}}\cong(J_C)_{k'}$ holds because the Picard
functor commutes with base change. Finally, $J_C$ is projective
by [lem-sc-abelian-variety-projective].

The hypothesis that $k$ is separably closed enters this proof exactly as in
the Picard chapter: it is what produces a $k$-rational point of $C$, from
which the representability theorem [thm-pc-picard-representable] of that
chapter deduces the fppf sheaf property of the naive Picard presheaf and hence
representability. For a curve over a general ground field the conclusion is
not asserted in this blueprint; see [rem-sc-jacobian-scope].
